name: MonarchHeatmap
title: Heatmap
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.Canvas with androidx.compose.ui.text.drawText and androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectTapGestures, inside MonarchChartFrame
summary: A matrix of values as shaded cells, such as activity by weekday and hour, with a Less to More legend.
whenToUse: To show where values cluster across two categories, such as weekday by hour or team by week.
whenNotToUse: To compare exact values, use a table or MonarchBarList. For one value per calendar day over months, use a calendar heatmap.
api: @Composable fun MonarchHeatmap(title: String, rows: List<MonarchHeatmapAxisItem>, columns: List<MonarchHeatmapAxisItem>, cells: List<MonarchHeatmapCell>, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, description: String? = null, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = MonarchChartFrameStatus.Ready, color: MonarchChartColor = MonarchChartColor.Data1, thresholds: List<Double>? = null, showValues: Boolean = false, showLegend: Boolean = true, summary: String? = null, emptyMessage: String? = null, footer: String? = null, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = null, onRetry: (() -> Unit)? = null, onSelect: ((MonarchHeatmapCell) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchHeatmapLabels = MonarchHeatmapLabels())
class MonarchHeatmapAxisItem(label: String, key: String = label)
class MonarchHeatmapCell(row: String, column: String, value: Double?, valueLabel: String? = null, note: String? = null)

class MonarchHeatmapLabels(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), rowHeader: String? = null, less: String? = null, more: String? = null, noData: String? = null, rangeBelow: String? = null, above: String? = null, range: String? = null, rangeAbove: String? = null, rowCount: ((rows: Int) -> String)? = null, columnCount: ((columns: Int) -> String)? = null, size: String? = null, highest: String? = null, cell: String? = null, withNote: String? = null, select: String? = null)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: cells
options.description: The values in any order. A row and column pair without a cell is no data.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: Ready, Loading, Empty or Error. A ready chart without any value shows the empty state.

options.name: color
options.description: The data color of the levels.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when null; a list of fewer than three is ignored.

options.name: showValues
options.description: Writes each value in its cell when the text fits in the cell at the current font size.

options.name: showLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the matrix.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that TalkBack reads for the matrix.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with the tapped cell, or the cell chosen with the TalkBack Select action; its value is null when it has no data.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are format strings with %1$s placeholders; the row and column counts are functions so they can follow the language's plural rules.

states.name: ready
states.description: Square cells in five levels: the muted background for zero, three mixes of the data color and the color itself, and an outlined cell for no data.

states.name: cell selected
states.description: A tapped cell gets a default-text outline, is marked selected for TalkBack, and its row, column and value are written under the matrix and announced politely.

states.name: values shown
states.description: Values are written in cells where the text fits; on the two strongest levels they sit on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists one row per heatmap row and one column per heatmap column, with notes.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no value.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Levels mix the chosen data color into the muted background at a quarter, half and three quarters, in Oklab, and use the color itself for the darkest step; zero is the muted background and no data is a subtle-border outline. Axis labels and the legend words are muted text; a selected cell is outlined in default text; values on strong levels sit on the surface color. The mix is computed from the theme's roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes keep five distinct steps.
platformNotes: The web Heatmap shows a tooltip on hover and moves an active cell with the arrow keys; on Android a tap selects a cell and its details are written under the matrix, and TalkBack moves through the cells row by row, each cell its own element. Cells are smaller than 48dp, so a cell is not a TalkBack button: with onSelect each cell has a Select custom action instead, while a finger taps anywhere on the matrix. iOS makes the matrix one adjustable element; Android has no equivalent that is not a slider. The web maxCellSize (36dp) and gap (2dp) are fixed here, the controlled activeCell is not offered, and the legend is not a separate public component. Column labels that would overlap are thinned to every second, third or later label. The iOS showsValues and showsLegend are showValues and showLegend, following Compose naming; the extra labels above and withNote cover text iOS builds in.
accessibility: The matrix is a traversal group whose content description is the generated summary (its size and its highest cell) or the summary given, with collection info of its rows and columns.
Every cell is a TalkBack element read as row, column and value with its note, in row order, with its row and column as collection item info, and the selected cell is marked selected.
With onSelect each cell has a Select custom action that selects it and calls onSelect.
The details of the selected cell are a polite live region that is always present, so each new selection is announced.
The legend is one element read as Legend followed by the range of each step, so the shades are not the only key.
The axis labels are hidden from TalkBack, as each cell names its row and column.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every value as text.
Axis labels, values and the legend scale with the font size; the chart measures its content and grows instead of cutting it.
edgeCases: Cells for keys that are not in rows or columns are ignored.
Two cells for the same position: the later one wins.
Negative values are level 0; values that are not finite are no data.
When every value is zero or less, every threshold is zero and any positive value is level 1.
Many columns make cells narrow, down to 4dp steps; column labels are thinned so they never overlap.
Row labels take at most 35% of the width and wrap beyond it.
A value is written in its cell only when its text fits inside the cell.

examples.title: Fixed thresholds, values in cells, selectable
examples.code:
MonarchHeatmap(
    title = "Hours logged",
    rows = listOf(MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("Design"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("Platform")),
    columns = listOf(MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W1"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W2"), MonarchHeatmapAxisItem("W3")),
    cells = listOf(
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row = "Design", column = "W1", value = 32.0),
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row = "Design", column = "W2", value = 38.0),
        MonarchHeatmapCell(row = "Platform", column = "W3", value = 41.0, valueLabel = "41h"),
    ),
    color = MonarchChartColor.Data2,
    thresholds = listOf(10.0, 25.0, 40.0),
    showValues = true,
    onSelect = { selected = "${it.row} ${it.column}" },
)
